proves.claim: a submit proof on any slot sets PULLBOARD_TEST_RESULT_STORE to the runner-wide pull-gate folder.

cli.io-submit-pull.proof-phase-shares-ru.why: Without it a repeat file on another slot reruns instead of reusing a stored green.

proves.claim: no shared store for the check role, a root with no pull folder, a landing shard, or an environment that already names one.

cli.io-submit-pull.shared-store-only-for.why: Without it a landing shard or an operator's own store setting could be overridden.

proves.claim: takeRunnerLock for one runner folder returns the lock first, then refuses RUNNER_ALREADY_RUNNING naming the first holder pid and how it was started.

cli.io-runner-lock.second-service-is-ref.why: Without it two services on one runner root each claim their own slots and double the load.

proves.claim: a lock file naming a pid that is not running, or whose start time does not match, is taken over and the new holder is recorded.

cli.io-runner-lock.dead-holder-is-taken-.why: Without it a crashed service would leave a lock that keeps every later service out.

proves.claim: runService takes the cache lock before it calls serve and, with the lock held, returns exit 1 with the RUNNER_ALREADY_RUNNING line without calling serve.

cli.io-runner-service.lock-held-exits-1-.why: Without it the second service would still serve the runner root.

proves.claim: With PULLBOARD_RUNNER_JOBS missing from the environment, the entry returns 1, never calls serve, and says a line naming PULLBOARD_RUNNER_JOBS and pullboard runner install-serve.

cli.io-runner-service.without-runner-job.why: Without it a service started without its slot count could fall to a cores-based default and starve gates.

proves.claim: With PULLBOARD_RUNNER_JOBS set to 10, the entry calls serve and returns 0, the path the installed launchd service takes.

cli.io-runner-service.with-runner-jobs-s.why: Without it the guard could refuse the installed service's own start.

proves.claim: composeSliceReview returns a review commit that contains the parent head plus each submitted slice's item_commit merged in slice id order.

cli.io-verify-slices.composes-parent-wit.why: Without it a parent review checks only the parent head and misses the slices that complete it.

proves.claim: A slice commit that conflicts with the composition refuses SLICE_COMPOSE naming that slice id, and no branch or ref is left behind.

cli.io-verify-slices.conflict-refuses-sl.why: Without it a conflicting slice would pass review silently or leave a half-composed branch.

proves.claim: With composeLanding true, an ACCEPT on a slice is SLICE_REVIEWED_WITH_PARENT and a REJECT on a slice is null.

cli.logic-slice-paths.slice-verdicts-wit.why: Without it a slice could be accepted alone, or a rejected slice could be blocked from returning to open by itself.

proves.claim: With composeLanding true, an ACCEPT on a parent with an unsubmitted slice is SLICES_PENDING; with it false every case is null.

cli.logic-slice-paths.parent-verdicts-an.why: Without it a parent could be accepted while a slice is still out, or the setting could change behaviour while off.

proves.claim: On a strict item verify accept without --broke is refused PROVEN_BREAK_REQUIRED and records nothing; with a 40-character --broke it accepts and the statement is on the item.

cli.io-commands-verify.strict-accept-nee.why: Without it a strict item could be accepted with no stated proof the reviewer broke it.

proves.claim: A reject needs no --broke even when the review requires a proven break.

cli.io-commands-verify.strict-reject-unc.why: Without it a reject could be blocked by the accept-only requirement.

proves.claim: A steady item with the setting unset accepts without --broke.

cli.io-commands-verify.steady-accept-unc.why: Without it the requirement could reach items that are not strict.

proves.claim: The real commit-msg hook refuses a 79-character header with its length and the limit and leaves the message file unchanged.

cli.hooks-main-part3.long-header-refused.why: Without it, a regression that cut the header or refused it without the length and limit would pass unnoticed.

proves.claim: The text resume names a row the person approved and spec apply has not written, with the apply next step.

cli.io-commands-resume.text-names-approv.why: Without it the text resume tells the coordinator to wait for an approval the person already gave.

proves.claim: The text resume stops naming a row once spec apply has written it.

cli.io-commands-resume.text-drops-row-af.why: Without it the coordinator keeps being told to apply a row that is already applied.

proves.claim: Resume --json prints a pendingApply array naming each approved row awaiting apply.

cli.io-commands-resume.json-pending-appl.why: Without it a JSON reader cannot see which approved rows wait for spec apply.

proves.claim: serveLocal throws LOCAL_RUNNER_RUNNING with a next line when a live runner already serves this home, so runner local exits non-zero.

cli.io-runner-local-serve.refusal-exits-.why: Without it a second runner local printed a success line and exited 0 while its board waited for a runner that never came.

proves.claim: ensureLocalRunner starts a runner and anyRunnerLive reports none for a home with no runner of its own while another home's runner is alive on the machine.

cli.io-runner-local-serve.other-home-get.why: Without it a second project on a machine with a runner never started one, and its jobs waited forever.

proves.claim: join in an already joined seat with another lane and the same model passes moveLane to register and reports moved from the old lane to the new one.

cli.io-commands-join.existing-seat-moves.why: Without it a seat could not return to the lane its item belongs to and join answered ALREADY_JOINED.

proves.claim: A LANE_HELD refusal from register is printed with its next line and a non-zero exit, and a different model still refuses ALREADY_JOINED.

cli.io-commands-join.move-refusal-reache.why: Without it a seat holding work could be moved silently, or a different model could take over a seat.

proves.claim: A pulled finish test job carries testResults naming its finish run and the selected files' ledger input keys, and its receipt's per-file rows are recorded under the proof command.

cli.io-test-pull.finish-run-carries-test.why: Without it a finish run's per-file passes never reach the proof ledger, so the gate runs again 34% of the files the finish run proved.

proves.claim: The per-file rows of a finish run's receipt are recorded in the board ledger, and the ledger then offers each of those files as a hit to the next run.

cli.io-test-pull.finish-rows-reach-ledge.why: Without it an unchanged file that a finish run proved would run again in the gate.

proves.claim: stats refusals counts the recorded refusals by code, highest first, with top seats and items, honours --since and carries the same rows in --json.

cli.io-commands-stats-refusals.counts-by.why: Without it, a regression where stats refusals counts the recorded refusals by code, highest first, with top seats and items, honours --since and carries the same rows in --json would pass unnoticed.

proves.claim: A --since that is not <number><s|m|h|d> refuses USAGE and an empty trace prints that nothing was recorded.

cli.io-commands-stats-refusals.refuses-a.why: Without it, a regression where a --since that is not <number><s|m|h|d> refuses USAGE and an empty trace prints that nothing was recorded would pass unnoticed.

proves.claim: unblockPlan counts live builder seats per route against buildable items per route, and traces stuck items through after chains and held parents to one root: a dead claim under a parent epic is the single root of 5 stuck items.

cli.logic-unblock.capacity-and-roots.why: Without it, a planner that stops at the first blocker or counts held items as buildable would pass unnoticed.

proves.claim: unblockPlan groups roots by cause, ranks them by the number of items each unblocks, and gives each the exact command that clears it.

cli.logic-unblock.ranked-actions.why: Without it, a wrong ranking or a wrong clearing command for a gate, hold, parent or re-scope root would pass unnoticed.

proves.claim: While another connection holds the board writer, next prints a finished test run and returns in under 200 ms, leaving the run undelivered.

cli.io-next-delivery.skips-busy-writer.why: Without it, next queues in the jobs store's write retry loop behind every verify, submit or release, and a builder waits seconds for a line it could print at once.

proves.claim: With the board writer free, next prints a finished test run and marks it delivered once; a second delivery prints nothing.

cli.io-next-delivery.marks-when-writer-f.why: Without it, skipping the write when the writer is busy could leave a run undelivered forever and reported on every next.

proves.claim: With 3,105 finished undelivered runs of other seats and the writer held, next's delivery step stays under 200 ms.

cli.io-next-delivery.cost-flat-with-run-.why: Without it, a delivery step that reads or writes other seats' runs would grow with the board's run history and pass on a small fixture.
